doc.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: How his parents met, being the eldest child, family addresses
summary: Johnson does not know how his parents met and defers to his sister Rosemary; he recalls the Indianapolis Avenue and North Capitol addresses.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: How did your mom and your dad meet?
Hmmm. I’m not quite sure that I ever knew the details of that question, Lida, I’m sorry to say. I’m sorry to disappoint you there.
Oh, heavens. It's not a disappointment. I was just wondering if your mom came to Indianapolis from Mississippi when she was an adult or if she was a child when she came to Indianapolis.
You know what’s interesting? I’ll tell you who knows and we should find out from her – my sister.

She’s very good on family history. I’m terrible. My memory disappoints me so often and so many times it’s embarrassing. My sister is very sharp on remembering things like what you are asking about. How did my mom and dad ever meet? She’ll tell you. I’ve go to find that out myself.
And once your mom and dad married and settled down and started a family, you were the first child in the family to be born?
And where did you live in Indianapolis at that time?

My earliest recollection, if you want to call it that, of living anywhere was 2337 Indianapolis Avenue. I don’t think I was born there, but I remember that because we lived there a very long time at 2337 Indianapolis Avenue. Later on there’s another address that – we moved four or five times in my lifetime that I can recall as a family. The only two addresses that stick out in my mind are 2337 Indianapolis Avenue and 1825
North Capitol, in later years. Right across from the hospital.
